findings.title: assets.css "non-empty" definition not pinned like js.src
findings.problem: The js.src 'non-empty' rule is pinned precisely (length > 0, no trimming, '  ' accepted) and tied to requireString, but the css section only says 'array of non-empty strings' without restating that same length>0/no-trim rule, risking an implementer rejecting whitespace-only css hrefs while accepting them for js.src despite both sharing validateAssets.
findings.fix: State explicitly that css 'non-empty' = length > 0 with no trimming, identical to js.src and applied by the same validateAssets string check; add a unit case css: ['  '] asserting it is accepted and escaped verbatim.

findings.title: assets.head empty-string entry behavior unspecified
findings.problem: head is specified only as 'array of strings' (no non-empty requirement unlike css/js.src), so head: [''] passes validation and emits a pure-indentation line; the design does not state whether an empty-string head entry is intended-legal or should be rejected.
findings.fix: State intent explicitly (recommended: empty strings are legal for the raw head passthrough and emit only the indentation line) and add a one-line unit assertion for head: [''] to lock the behavior.
